question.problem:
The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ is shown below. Which of the points shown are the local maxima of the function?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227500/assets/245ba0a543188d50e52c23c854f9f82290790ed715c241bf27e505b04d857a4e.png)
question.worked_solution:
Consider the point $U.$ We can take an open interval of $x$-values such that $U$ will be the highest point on the graph in this interval. So, $U$ is a local maximum.

A similar interval exists for the point $W,$ too. So, $W$ is also a local maximum.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14227500/assets/ac0a6e28e4564883e6743b2d600cb8611723e813e85c1acb5fcc327ee3dbc9b5.png)
